title: Better together: Reciprocal activation of quorum sensing circuits enhances bacterial communication
content:
by Andrew Frando, Ajai A. Dandekar, Josephine R. Chandler

Many bacteria use quorum sensing to control gene transcription based on population density. A recent study in PLOS Biology found that in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, two quorum sensing circuits activate each other, enhancing robustness and explaining their redundancy.
